retained_original_metadata.title: Every finite-dimensional transitive real Lie algebra of smooth local vector fields that is solvable admits local nonnegative weighted coordinates with nonpositive-degree fields and a finite-dimensional commutative degree-zero part
retained_original_metadata.author: Katarzyna Grabowska; Janusz Grabowski
retained_original_metadata.source_title: Solvable Lie Algebras of Vector Fields and a Lie's Conjecture
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The obligation is a constructive local normal form for an arbitrary transitive solvable action, where its nilradical need not be transitive. The proof assembles coordinates along a nested regular foliation, descends the action through the last abelian leaves, and controls coefficient weights by an induction on bracket differentiation. This goes substantially beyond Lie’s theorem for finite-dimensional matrix representations or routine straightening of a single vector field.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The complete constructive proof of Theorem 4.1 was read with Proposition 3.7 and the nilradical filtration in Section 3. The author constructs local coordinates through successively closed quotient one-forms, straightens the final abelian foliation, descends to a lower-dimensional transitive solvable algebra, and uses bracket differentiation to bound the weights of the remaining coefficients. The previously published nilpotent-coordinate theorem (Theorem 2.3, credited to [11]) is genuine background for the nilradical leaves; the new solvable induction is supplied here. Only the finite-dimensional smooth local statement is selected, not the later infinite-dimensional analytic extension or Lie-conjecture consequence.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem 4.1 for finite-dimensional real solvable transitive Lie algebras of smooth vector fields in a neighbourhood U of 0 in R^n. The nilradical series L^0=L, L^1=nr(L), L^(j+1)=[nr(L),L^j] determines nonnegative integer weights and multiplicities from its foliation dimension drops. In suitable local coordinates L lies in g^{<=0}(U,h), L^j lies in degrees <=-j, and L is contained in g^{<0}(U,h) plus a finite-dimensional commutative degree-zero subalgebra. No global coordinate system, classification, analytic infinite-dimensional extension, or separate Lie-conjecture theorem is claimed.
retained_original_metadata.editorial_warning: Editorial typography notice, separate from the author proof: the Section 3 sentence after (3.4) writes b_j=dim F^{r_j}, but the very next displayed filtration explicitly uses leaf dimension n-b_j; throughout the construction b_j=a_1+...+a_j is the number of coordinates already chosen. Proposition 3.7(5) also prints b_(m-1)=k-a_m where the established dimension is n-a_m. These isolated dimension-letter slips are retained in the source; the named coordinate ranges and dimension-drop definitions fix the interpretation. The proof describes a transversal “curve” when choosing the leafwise additive constants; it uses the previously established tuple u of transverse parameters, so this is the local transversal in those parameters.
